scoring_justification: T0 result‑level compare: the raw artifact is only the final R values; no intermediate parameters are public to recompute from. The checker compares the agent's R values against digitized reference values from the paper's Figure 2 (relative tolerance 5%) and verifies monotonic descent with wavelength.

outputs.description: Computed power reflection coefficient R for normal-incidence H-polarized plane waves on metal-wire gratings of period 8 mm, thickness 2 mm, slot width δ ranging from 1 to 6 mm, at wavelengths 50, 70, 90, 120 mm.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference R values for value‑match check against the agent's computed reflection_coefficients.csv
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Digitized from Figure 2 of the paper 'Use of periodic structures to produce standard measures of reflection coefficient' (Measurement Techniques, 1994). The curves are experimentally measured and, according to the paper, agree with the theoretical calculation to within about 5% for wavelengths > 40 mm.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Manual digitization of the measured curves in the paper's Figure 2 at specified wavelengths and slot widths. The absolute values were read from the graph with estimated precision of ±2% relative.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are not random numbers; they are approximate values extracted from the published figure of the paper to serve as a hidden sanity reference. They are consistent with the paper's description that R decreases with increasing wavelength and covers a wide dynamic range across slot widths.

steps.description: Check that R decreases monotonically as wavelength increases for each slot width δ.
